statusScale.IMPLEMENTED_NOT_VERIFIED: Source changed; no test of the behaviour on file.
statusScale.UNIT_VERIFIED: Positive and adversarial tests pass against mocks or an in-process SQL engine. No deployed row-level security was involved.
statusScale.NATIVE_VERIFIED: The repaired code ran unmodified against real PostgreSQL 15 and 16 with the combined deployed schema, runtime role and row-level security, with an adversarial cross-tenant case.
statusScale.E2E_VERIFIED: Proven through the running application over HTTP or a browser, through the proxy and routing layer.
statusScale.CLOSED: Every proof the acceptance condition requires is on file and an independent release decision has been made.

PATCH /api/grievances/[id]/assign cannot assign an escalated grievance to a text-id representative. Root cause (traced, not yet fixed): the route validates stewardId as a GUID and uses the SAME value as a steward RECORD id (stewards.id, in assignSteward and steward_assignments, with a caseload counter) and as a user PRINCIPAL (assignPrimaryRepresentative, grievances.union_rep_id). Kernel principals are text, while grievances.union_rep_id is uuid; that column is referenced by 51 files (queries, pglite suites, the Django backend). The fix is a coordinated one: a text principal for the assignment input, a lookup from principal to steward record for the caseload bookkeeping (skipped when no record exists), and a migration of union_rep_id to text with its Django model and readers. It is deliberately not a partial change. Related to R-29
Two audit stores: kernel authority events are written to public.audit_logs and route audits to audit_security.audit_logs (different column sets); reporting must read both

ORM/physical parity sweep: 662 NOT NULL columns in 216 tables have no database default while the ORM emits DEFAULT (class of R-16; organization_members and grievances fixed). Evidence: docs/union-eyes/convergence/evidence/vs-orm-physical-parity-eba009ba6.json

Principal columns declared text in the ORM but uuid in the database. 15 of 16 are now fixed: migration 0033 (nine columns of the three external representation tables) and migration 0034 (six columns: employer_communications sender_user_id and created_by, employer_contacts.created_by, ai_grievance_triages.reviewed_by, ai_clause_reasonings.reviewed_by, ai_copilot_sessions.user_id), each proven on native PG15 and PG16 (7 tests each, including the combined database where it applied for real) and re-measured with the parity tool (evidence/vs-orm-physical-parity-after-0034.json). ONE remains: cookie_consents.user_id is a foreign key to profiles(id) (uuid), so retyping it would remove referential integrity or require a principal-to-profile mapping: a product decision, left unchanged. Non-principal entity id columns (ORM text, database uuid) are a separate, lower-risk class

The proxy mutation limiter was dead code for any request without an Idempotency-Key (an early return preceded it) and, where reachable, was keyed on a client-supplied x-org-id header: a client escaped it by omitting a header, and a caller of one tenant exhausted another tenant's bucket (the legitimate victim received 429). Replaced by an API guard keyed on the presented credential and the client address, covering every API request including public routes. Demonstrated on the vulnerable build, fixed, and re-proven over HTTP

Public API routes and several raw-handler write routes had no rate limit of their own (the guard now covers them at the edge); per-route limits for abuse-sensitive public endpoints (public intake, sign-up) and per-user limits for expensive operations should be reviewed route by route

Auditor duties were unreachable over HTTP. The finance routes keep their frozen role allow-list (pinned by the Financial Officer contract, so not loosened). A separate read-only route, GET /api/assurance/finance/ledger, now serves the independent auditor: authority is a live financial mandate holding the audit power on the organization ledger, issued through the governed workflow; every read is audited; it accepts no write. Verified over HTTP on the production build (spec 08: the auditor reads and the read is audited; the audit duty confers nothing else; finance duties, an auditor-titled user without a mandate, approver, administrator, executive, steward, member, another tenant, platform identity and unauthenticated caller are refused; revocation removes access at once and restoration reissues it). Trustees are NOT exercised: there is no trustee role in the platform role model and no trustee route

Authority-kernel bootstrap gap: the auditor and trustee capacities are appointment-only (earned from a live mandate), yet issuing the first financial mandate requires the holder to ALREADY hold one of financial_officer, executive, trustee or auditor. A genuinely independent person with only the member capacity can therefore never be appointed auditor or trustee through the kernel. The QA auditor fixture works around it by carrying the executive capacity through its stored role (disclosed in tests/fixtures/test-users.ts) and holds only the audit power. A product decision is needed on how an independent auditor is first appointed (for example a governed appointment instrument that confers the capacity); the issuance policy was not changed

External counsel cannot be granted access through the product. (1) No HTTP route issues, activates or revokes a representation authority or an external matter grant: the service functions exist but are wired to no route, so the legacy external routes are readable only for rows inserted directly into the database. (2) Two overlapping external-access designs exist: the legacy representation_authorities / matter-grant tables behind /api/external/*, and the kernel counsel engagement register, whose model is that counsel works in a SEPARATE system and the union only receives signed assertions. (3) The kernel assertion verifier is an injected port with no implementation, so every counsel assertion is refused. Which model is canonical is a product decision; building issuance on the legacy model would extend the second design, so it was not built. Spec 09 proves the READ side only, against a labelled synthetic database fixture (scripts/runtime/external-admin.ts)

FIXED for the session and identity-provider paths, proven over HTTP. Root cause (found by tracing, not the first hypothesis): getCurrentUser() resolved the role from the identity provider, and an identity that asserts no role (the QA acceptance session, a provider without role claims) defaulted to member, so every withRoleAuth route above the member floor (55 routes) refused every caller. The role now comes from the caller's own active membership, read inside that organization's RLS context (a bare connection matches no row), only when the identity asserts none; no membership still means member, and an asserted role is never overridden. Verified: spec 10 (administrator reaches /api/docs, the pilot telemetry routes and organization settings; steward passes the steward role gate; member, steward and executive are refused where they must be) plus 6 unit tests. NOT proven: the real password-session path, which cannot run (R-43)

Real password login cannot run in the orchestrator's runtime (POST /api/auth/login returns 500: AUTH_DATABASE_URL, the dedicated auth-gateway role, is not provisioned). An attempt to provision it in that database was made and DELIBERATELY ABANDONED: the legacy-bootstrapped database is not a valid canonical topology (R-45) and the application's own catalog admission rejects it, correctly failing closed. The real login path IS exercised by the existing canonical V2 acceptance harness (next-acceptance.ts), whose evidence is recorded separately (evidence/vs-v2-real-login-smoke.json) and must not be merged with the synthetic-session runtime evidence. Remaining: that harness still ends FAIL (R-46)

crud-factory DELETE hard-coded an administrator floor and ignored writeRole, so on a table whose writes are reserved for an elevated role an organization administrator could still delete any row by id. Found by promoting DEF-0B12-CRUD-TESTIMONIAL-ITEM-WRITES to HTTP: the historical repair raised the PATCH floor to content_manager but left DELETE at admin, and the route unit tests mocked the factory away and could not see it. Demonstrated on the pre-fix production build (the administrator's DELETE was not refused), fixed (delete floor is the higher of administrator and the write role), and re-run green. A unit test now inspects the factory's real floors (it fails without the fix). Other tables with an elevated writeRole share the factory: arbitration precedents and search (content_manager), data-classification policy (compliance_manager) and security events (security_manager)

The orchestrator's legacy-bootstrapped database cannot host the canonical authentication topology. Found by trying to provision the nzila_auth_* gateway roles in it: oauth_providers sits in public (canonical: user_management); magic_links lacks three nullable columns the canonical declaration has (requested_ip, consumed_ip, requested_user_agent); platform_identity_bindings does not exist; legacy bootstrap policies on the auth tables block the canonical bootstrap ("explicit reconciliation"); and after forced reconciliation the application's catalog admission still rejected it (legacy catalog contract vs canonical auth grants). So the QA runtime and the V2 topology are two different systems, and everything proven in the QA runtime is evidence about the legacy topology only

The canonical V2 acceptance ends FAIL on its last step: the application's own catalog admission rejects the V2 database with 25 violations (evidence/vs-v2-real-login-smoke.json lists them): union_eyes_runtime holds schema USAGE on user_management; deadline_reassignment_convergence, document_versions, donations, evidence_packs, geofence_events, location_deletion_log, location_tracking and message_threads carry privileges or policies the contract does not match; ue_v2_bootstrap_receipt is unclassified; commercial_contracts and external_data_sync_log carry unapproved column ACLs for union_eyes_system; nzila_auth_system_mutation lacks its organization_members column grants; and the case-assignee and conversation-assignee predicate functions are missing from the V2 build. The V2 source plan has drifted from the catalog contract. The plan is a frozen digest-bound artifact, so this needs a deliberate plan regeneration, not an ad hoc patch. ROOT CAUSE FOUND (not yet fixed): the plan embeds a STALE snapshot of the storage-authority manifest. For example its deadline_reassignment_convergence authority still carries the old "system-only D1" text and grants runtime nothing, while the manifest was reclassified on 2026-10-21 to runtime SELECT/INSERT (the assign route inserts the convergence task inside the tenant transaction), and the manifest and the digest-pinned catalog contract agree with each other on the 8 flagged tables. So admission is right and the plan is behind. Two further causes are independent of the plan: the canonical overlay leaves the runtime schema-USAGE contract at its legacy value although the canonical auth topology requires runtime USAGE on user_management, and the V2 bootstrap receipt table is unclassified. Regenerating the plan needs the hash-pinned offline wheelhouse, which was built from requirements.lock outside the repository (87 wheels). A fast reproduction (scripts/runtime/v2-admission-probe.ts) yields exactly the harness's 25 violations in about two minutes

Under the canonical V2 topology every kernel-decided route returned 500: the authority kernel read membership straight from user_management.organization_users, but the V2 runtime role holds no grant on the identity relations ("permission denied for table organization_users"). The reader-owned SECURITY DEFINER source (membershipSourceViaDefiner, compileAuthorityMembershipReaderSql) existed only in native and in-process tests and was neither installed by the V2 bootstrap nor used by the application. Found by the V2 real-login acceptance (a steward's POST /api/claims). Fixed: an activeMembershipSource selects the definer function under V2 and the direct read on the legacy lineage (3 unit tests); the V2 installer now installs the reader function and its expectation is registered with the catalog contract. Verified: the V2 acceptance steps steward-claim-create (200), member-claim-create-denied (403) and role-revoked-claim-create-denied (403) pass over the real login path. Two in-process suites that mock V2 over a legacy-shaped database were adapted to read membership directly (disclosed)

Catalog admission raised on a topology without an audit_security schema (has_schema_privilege on a missing schema), failing the whole admission instead of reporting violations; it now inspects only schemas that exist. Whether the V2 topology should HAVE an audit_security schema (the ORM audit writers target it) is not decided. Separately the V2 smoke's ordinary-preference-write step was stale: the route now refuses client-supplied organizationId and userId with 400. The step now asserts that refusal and that nothing was persisted, then performs the legitimate write (a strengthening of a historical acceptance step, disclosed)

The disposable runtime published its services on every interface: the orchestrator ran Postgres with -p 55430:5432 and Next on all interfaces, and the native-sweep helper did the same with a fixed password. Now Postgres, Redis, the native PG15/PG16 containers and the app (next start --hostname 127.0.0.1) all bind IPv4 loopback only, and every URL uses 127.0.0.1. Side effect found and resolved: once a container is published on IPv4 loopback only, "localhost" resolves to ::1 first on this Windows host and connections stall, which made the Django-audit native suite hang for ~400 s and fail 3 of 4; with explicit 127.0.0.1 it passes 4 of 4 in 18 s. That was an artefact of my own change, not a product regression. Verified: full runtime suite 110 passed, 0 failed on the loopback-only stack. NOT changed: an unrelated container ue-local-pg that this work did not create is still published on 0.0.0.0:55440; it was left alone and is flagged for its owner

Measured whole app: 1,522 files passed, 4 skipped, 21,073 tests passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed. The driver contract step failed 2 tests only because bash resolved to the WSL relay; with Git bash the contract suite passes 302 files / 10,280 tests. Unit-level proof only
